_readme: Every modelling assumption lives here. Edit freely; the engine and the web interface read these as defaults. Each block has a _why explaining the choice and what would replace it with better data.

colour._why: How a shirt becomes a card colour. rule 'dominant' is the original game: each card has ONE colour, the colour family covering most of the shirt (body 70%, sleeves 15% each, stripes measured from pattern images). If two colours are within tie_tolerance of each other, the one earlier in tie_priority wins (chromatic colours before white/black/grey). rule 'all' is a variant where every colour covering at least min_share of the shirt counts. 'basic' scheme merges navy/sky into blue and claret into red; 'detailed' keeps them apart.

kit_usage._why: Share of a team's matches played in each kit. No global per-match kit database exists, so this is an ESTIMATE: home kit = all home games + away games without a colour clash; away = clashes; third = double clashes and promotional games. Replace with real counts per team in data/overrides/kit_usage_overrides.json when available (e.g. World Cup match pages list kits worn).

matches_per_season._why: How many matches a team plays per season; scales how often its shirts are seen. Club figures = league games + typical cups by league level; national teams play ~10 a year.

popularity._why: Card decks over-represent famous teams. Popularity = number of Wikipedia language editions with an article on the team (Wikidata sitelinks), a proxy for global fame. weight = matches x popularity^exponent. Turn off for a 'whole football world' deck.

deck_population._why: Which teams can appear on cards.

game._why: Rules as described: 2 players, deck split evenly, reorder only between sets, winner of a set starts the next one, match = at least one shared shirt colour, you lose when you must play and have no cards.
